note: The compiled PHP input controls the CV operand for the object property write expression and supplies the object stored in container.

code: zend_fetch_property_address(result, container, IS_CV, property, IS_CONST, CACHE_ADDR(opline->extended_value & ~ZEND_FETCH_OBJ_FLAGS), BP_VAR_W, opline->extended_value & ZEND_FETCH_OBJ_FLAGS, 1 OPLINE_CC EXECUTE_DATA_CC);
note: The write-fetch opcode forwards the input-controlled object and property name into the property address helper.
The helper extracts the zend_object pointer that will be used by the standard property handler.

Creating an undeclared dynamic property emits a deprecation warning and invokes user error handling while the handler still plans to use zobj afterward, but it does not keep the object alive across that callback.
After the error handler can remove the last PHP reference to the object, this dereference of zobj reads from the freed object storage.
